title: First Investigation of Deep Learning for Intraoperative Gauze Segmentation in Minimally Invasive Abdominal Surgery
summary: Surgical gauze is an essential part of surgical procedures, primarily used for controlling bleeding and absorbing bodily fluids. The post-surgical retention of gauze can lead to serious complications and necessitate additional surgery for its removal. Despite the clinical significance, research on gauze segmentation using real-world surgical data remains underexplored, owing in part to the scarcity of annotated datasets. In this work, we investigate the use of deep learning methods for gauze segmentation in robot-assisted minimally invasive abdominal surgeries, utilizing an in-house surgical dataset prepared at a university hospital. The training data reflects realistic surgical settings and captures extensive diversity in spatial, morphological, and visual attributes across three different gauze categories. We evaluate several widely used segmentation architectures, including CNN-based, transformer-based, and hybrid architectures, to establish a proof-of-concept for gauze segmentation in a realistic clinical setting. In addition, we investigate the influence of sub-optimally annotated, auto-tracked segmentation masks as a strategy to address data scarcity and improve performance. Our results demonstrate the efficacy of real-world training data in countering the main challenge reported by prior works, the trade-off between blood presence and gauze detection. The incorporation of auto-tracked annotations yields performance enhancements, particularly in generic surgical scenarios. The integration of effective segmentation approaches can benefit robot-guided surgical procedures and various downstream applications by providing precise delineation of foreign objects, thereby enhancing patient safety and surgical outcomes.
tldr: This paper presents the first investigation of deep learning methods for intraoperative gauze segmentation in robot-assisted minimally invasive abdominal surgery, using a real-world surgical dataset and evaluating various architectures to address the challenge of detecting gauze in the presence of blood.
tldr_zh: 本文首次研究了在机器人辅助微创腹部手术中，利用深度学习进行术中纱布分割的方法，使用真实手术数据集评估多种架构，以解决血液存在下纱布检测的挑战。
summary_zh: 手术纱布是外科手术中的关键组成部分，主要用于控制出血和吸收体液。术后纱布遗留可能导致严重并发症，并需再次手术取出。尽管具有临床重要性，但利用真实手术数据进行纱布分割的研究仍处于探索阶段，部分原因在于标注数据集的稀缺。本研究探索了在机器人辅助微创腹部手术中应用深度学习方法进行纱布分割，使用某大学医院自建的手术数据集。训练数据反映了真实手术场景，并涵盖了三种不同纱布类别在空间、形态和视觉属性上的广泛多样性。我们评估了多种主流分割架构，包括基于CNN、基于Transformer以及混合架构，以在真实临床环境中为纱布分割建立概念验证。此外，我们研究了次优标注及自动追踪分割掩膜作为应对数据稀缺并提升性能策略的影响。结果表明，使用真实训练数据能够有效应对既往研究报告的主要挑战——血液存在与纱布检测之间的权衡。融入自动追踪标注能够提升性能，尤其在通用手术场景中。整合有效的分割方法可通过精准勾勒异物轮廓，助力机器人引导手术流程及各类下游应用，从而提升患者安全性与手术效果。

title: TAVI-TEC: An AI-Based Tool for Procedural Planning of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation
summary: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preprocedural TAVI planning, providing the anatomical information required for prosthesis sizing and vascular access assessment. As the volume of TAVI procedure increases, improving efficiency and standardizing annotations is becoming essential in clinical practice. This study presents TAVI-TEC, a fully automated artificial intelligence-based framework integrated into a web based DICOM viewer for routine preoperative TAVI planning. Pre-procedural CTA scans from patients undergoing TAVI with SAPIEN 3 Ultra (S3U) prostheses were processed using a fully automated pipeline. Deep learning-based segmentation of cardiovascular structures, calcification detection, centerline extraction, landmark identification, and annular plane definition was implemented to quantify key annular and aortic root measurements and color-coded maps of lumen reduction and vessel diameter for vascular access. A multilayer perceptron classifier was trained to predict prosthesis size prior to the TAVI procedure. Results revealed that TAVI-TEC enabled pre-procedural measurements in approximately 2-6 min. Strong agreement with clinician-derived measurements was observed for annular area (coefficient of concordance, CCC = 0.934; interclass correlation coefficient, ICC = 0.935; R^2 = 0.881) and perimeter (CCC = 0.909; ICC = 0.909; R^2 = 0.854). The valve-size prediction model achieved 82% overall accuracy, with most misclassifications occurring between adjacent prosthesis sizes. Though further multicenter validation and extension to additional measurements and valve platforms are required, the TAVI-TEC methodology may reduce operator variability in pre-TAVI measurements and streamline the preoperative workflows of the Heart Team for decision-making.
tldr: TAVI-TEC is a fully automated AI framework integrated into a web-based DICOM viewer for preprocedural TAVI planning, using deep learning for segmentation and a multilayer perceptron for valve-size prediction, achieving 82% accuracy and reducing processing time to 2-6 minutes.
tldr_zh: TAVI-TEC是一个集成到基于Web的DICOM查看器中的全自动AI框架，用于TAVI术前规划，利用深度学习进行分割，并使用多层感知器进行瓣膜尺寸预测，准确率达82%，处理时间缩短至2-6分钟。
summary_zh: 计算机断层扫描血管造影（CTA）对于经导管主动脉瓣植入术（TAVI）的术前规划至关重要，可提供假体尺寸选择和血管入路评估所需的解剖信息。随着TAVI手术量的增加，提高效率并标准化标注在临床实践中变得日益重要。本研究提出TAVI-TEC，这是一个完全自动化的人工智能框架，集成于基于网络的DICOM查看器中，用于常规术前TAVI规划。研究处理了接受SAPIEN 3 Ultra（S3U）假体TAVI患者的术前CTA扫描数据，采用全自动处理流程。通过基于深度学习的算法实现心血管结构分割、钙化检测、中心线提取、标志点识别以及瓣环平面定义，从而量化关键的瓣环和主动脉根部测量指标，并生成用于血管入路的管腔缩减与血管直径彩色编码图。训练了一个多层感知器分类器，用于在TAVI术前预测假体尺寸。结果显示，TAVI-TEC可在约2-6分钟内完成术前测量。在瓣环面积（一致性系数CCC=0.934；组内相关系数ICC=0.935；R²=0.881）和周长（CCC=0.909；ICC=0.909；R²=0.854）方面，与临床医生测量结果高度一致。瓣膜尺寸预测模型的总体准确率达82%，大多数误判发生在相邻假体尺寸之间。尽管需要进一步的多中心验证以及扩展到更多测量指标和瓣膜平台，但TAVI-TEC方法可减少术前TAVI测量中的操作者差异，并优化心脏团队的术前决策工作流程。

title: Leveraging Transfer Learning with Class-Specific Decoders for Laparoscopic Segmentation
summary: Effective multi-organ segmentation in surgical data requires learning the intricate anatomical features and alleviating the challenge of class imbalance, which results from relatively lower proportions of small and limitedly exposed structures. Recent works on laparoscopic multi-organ segmentation focus on learning structure-specific features through class-specific decoder architectures and report favorable results. This work extends the decoder-focused architectures to investigate knowledge sharing in the cross-surgical domain. We utilize two datasets representing different surgical domains, rectal and cholecystectomy surgeries, to explore how surgical conceptual knowledge transfers under partially common anatomical representations. Additionally, we compare the feature adaptation for the encoder and decoder at different training stages to analyse the knowledge adaptation and retention in the network. Our results corroborate previous findings on decoder-specific architectures and demonstrate that the organ-specific decoder model (CEMD), fully fine-tuned after cross-domain pre-training, achieves the highest segmentation performance (62.4\% dice) while converging substantially faster than training from scratch. However, we also find that class imbalance in surgical data remains a persistent challenge that transfer learning does not fully resolve for underrepresented anatomical structures.
tldr: This paper investigates transfer learning with class-specific decoders for multi-organ segmentation in laparoscopic surgery, showing that cross-domain pre-training with fully fine-tuned organ-specific decoders (CEMD) achieves the best performance (62.4% Dice) and faster convergence, though class imbalance remains a challenge.
tldr_zh: 本文研究了在腹腔镜手术多器官分割中结合类别特定解码器的迁移学习，结果表明跨域预训练后对器官特定解码器（CEMD）进行全微调可获得最佳性能（Dice 62.4%）且收敛更快，但类别不平衡问题仍未完全解决。
summary_zh: 在手术数据中实现有效的多器官分割需要学习复杂的解剖特征，并缓解因小型及暴露有限结构占比较低而导致的类别不平衡挑战。近期关于腹腔镜多器官分割的研究聚焦于通过类别特定的解码器架构学习结构特异性特征，并取得了良好结果。本研究将解码器导向架构延伸至跨手术领域的知识共享探究。我们利用代表不同手术领域（直肠手术与胆囊切除术）的两个数据集，探索手术概念知识如何在部分共同的解剖表征下实现迁移。此外，我们比较了不同训练阶段下编码器与解码器的特征适应情况，以分析网络中的知识适应与保留机制。我们的结果印证了先前关于解码器特异性架构的发现，并表明经过跨域预训练后完全微调的器官特异性解码器模型（CEMD）取得了最高分割性能（62.4% Dice），且收敛速度显著快于从头训练。然而，我们也发现手术数据中的类别不平衡仍是持续性挑战，迁移学习未能完全解决代表性不足的解剖结构这一问题。

title: DynoDINO: Harnessing Dynamic Latent Information from DINO Features for Multi-Phase Medical Image Segmentation
summary:
Multi-phase Contrast-Enhanced Computed Tomography (CECT) plays a central role in the diagnosis and characterization of focal lesions by capturing temporal enhancement patterns across multiple acquisition phases. Accurate lesion segmentation from such data remains challenging because clinically relevant contrast kinetics are distributed across phases, while anatomical inconsistencies, respiratory motion, and incomplete acquisitions often lead to inter-phase misalignment and interrupted temporal information. Conventional segmentation frameworks typically process each phase independently or rely on simple fusion strategies, limiting their temporal reasoning capability.
  To address these challenges, we propose DynoDINO, a unified framework tailored to address the core challenges of multi-phase medical image segmentation. DynoDINO first performs slice-level alignment to establish inter-phase anatomical correspondence and then employs a Multi-phase Fusion Model to jointly enhance temporal correlations across phases. Our fusion model incorporates a Mix-attention (MA) mechanism for efficient multi-phase feature calibration and an Adaptive Gating Mechanism with difference-based residual learning to selectively preserve diagnostically relevant contrast variations while suppressing artifacts caused by residual misalignment. In addition, the adaptive gating mechanism improves training stability by preventing feature degradation caused by unguided subtraction operations.
  Experiments on three large-scale datasets, including LiTS, PLC-CECT, and WAW-TACE, demonstrate that DynoDINO consistently improves boundary delineation and structural fidelity under standard, shifted, and missing-phase conditions.
tldr: DynoDINO proposes a unified framework for multi-phase CECT lesion segmentation that aligns slices across phases and fuses temporal information using a Mix-attention mechanism and adaptive gating with difference-based residual learning, achieving improved boundary delineation under standard and challenging conditions.
tldr_zh: DynoDINO提出了一种统一的多相CECT病灶分割框架，通过跨相位切片对齐，并利用混合注意力机制和基于差异残差学习的自适应门控融合时序信息，在标准及缺失相位条件下提升了边界描绘质量。
summary_zh:
多期对比增强计算机断层扫描（CECT）通过捕获多个采集期相中的时间增强模式，在局灶性病变的诊断与特征描述中发挥核心作用。然而，基于此类数据实现精确的病变分割仍具挑战性，因为临床相关的对比剂动力学分布在不同期相中，而解剖结构不一致、呼吸运动及采集不完整常导致期相间错位和时间信息中断。传统分割框架通常独立处理每个期相或依赖简单的融合策略，限制了其时间推理能力。

为解决上述问题，我们提出DynoDINO——一个专为应对多期医学图像分割核心挑战而设计的统一框架。DynoDINO首先执行切片级对齐以建立期相间的解剖对应关系，随后采用多期融合模型联合增强跨期相的时间相关性。该融合模型集成了混合注意力机制以实现高效的多期特征校准，以及基于差异残差学习的自适应门控机制——可选择性地保留诊断相关的对比度变化，同时抑制残余错位导致的伪影。此外，自适应门控机制通过防止无引导减法操作引发的特征退化，提升了训练稳定性。

在LiTS、PLC-CECT和WAW-TACE三个大规模数据集上的实验表明，DynoDINO在标准、偏移及缺失期相条件下均能持续改善边界勾勒与结构保真度。

title: UltraSAM3: A Concept-Driven Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Image Segmentation
summary: Ultrasound imaging has become increasingly widespread in clinical practice due to its portability, low cost and real-time capability, making ultrasound image segmentation important. However, ultrasound images differ substantially from CT, MRI, and other medical imaging modalities, as they are often affected by speckle noise, low contrast, acoustic shadows and ambiguous boundaries. Existing ultrasound segmentation methods are still mainly limited to task-specific models or visual-prompt-based foundation models, which are either tailored to particular tasks or require expert-provided visual prompts, making them inconvenient for flexible clinical use. To address these challenges, we propose UltraSAM3, a concept-driven foundation model for universal ultrasound image segmentation. Unlike conventional models, UltraSAM3 enables text-based target specification by adapting SAM3 to ultrasound-specific image--mask--concept triplets. The model is trained on a large-scale ultrasound segmentation corpus covering 37 public datasets and 13 anatomical categories, allowing it to align ultrasound visual patterns with clinically meaningful concepts across diverse organs and lesions. To further improve usability under realistic clinical interaction, we propose an instruction-guided agent that parses complex natural language queries into concise ultrasound concept prompts for UltraSAM3. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UltraSAM3 consistently outperforms representative concept- and text-driven biomedical segmentation models on multi-organ ultrasound benchmarks, external datasets, and visual-prompt-enhanced settings. Moreover, the agent improves segmentation robustness for complex user instructions. These results indicate that ultrasound-specific concept adaptation is effective for building generalizable and interactive ultrasound segmentation foundation models.
tldr: UltraSAM3 adapts SAM3 to ultrasound imaging by training on a large corpus of image-mask-concept triplets, enabling text-based target specification for universal segmentation, and introduces an instruction-guided agent to parse complex queries, achieving superior performance on multi-organ benchmarks.
tldr_zh: UltraSAM3通过在大规模超声图像-掩膜-概念三元组上训练，将SAM3适配到超声成像，实现基于文本的目标指定进行通用分割，并引入指令引导代理解析复杂查询，在多器官基准上取得优越性能。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
超声成像因其便携性、低成本及实时能力在临床实践中日益普及，这使得超声图像分割变得尤为重要。然而，超声图像与CT、MRI等其他医学影像模态存在显著差异，常受到散斑噪声、低对比度、声影及模糊边界的影响。现有超声分割方法仍主要局限于任务特定模型或基于视觉提示的基础模型，这些模型要么针对特定任务定制，要么需要专家提供视觉提示，导致其在灵活临床应用中不便。为应对这些挑战，我们提出UltraSAM3——一种面向通用超声图像分割的概念驱动基础模型。与传统模型不同，UltraSAM3通过将SAM3适配于超声特有的图像—掩膜—概念三元组，实现了基于文本的目标指定。该模型在覆盖37个公开数据集和13个解剖类别的大规模超声分割语料库上进行训练，使其能够将超声视觉模式与跨不同器官及病变的临床意义概念对齐。为进一步提升真实临床交互场景下的可用性，我们提出一种指令引导代理，可将复杂自然语言查询解析为UltraSAM3的简洁超声概念提示。大量实验表明，UltraSAM3在多器官超声基准、外部数据集及视觉提示增强设置中始终优于具有代表性的概念驱动及文本驱动生物医学分割模型。此外，该代理提高了针对复杂用户指令的分割鲁棒性。这些结果表明，超声特异性概念适配对于构建可泛化且可交互的超声分割基础模型是有效的。

title: Few-shot Deep Learning for Phase-Amplitude Aberration Correction in Transcranial Focused Ultrasound
summary: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) is a non-invasive technique that delivers focused acoustic energy through the skull for neuromodulation and therapeutic applications. However, the heterogeneous structure of the skull induces complex, patient-specific phase and amplitude aberrations that distort the acoustic focus and deviate it from the intended target, compromising therapeutic efficacy and safety. Conventional time-reversal (TR) simulations can correct these aberrations but rely on computationally expensive full-wave solvers, making them impractical for real-time use and iterative treatment planning. We propose a few-shot deep surrogate framework that predicts per-element phase and amplitude corrections for a 96-element 3D phased-array transducer from patient CT images. A geometry-aware encoder extracts skull-path features shared across dedicated phase classification and amplitude regression branches, where phase periodicity is handled via circular expectation decoding. The framework is pretrained on diverse skull geometries and fine-tuned with only ten target points, enabling rapid adaptation to unseen patients without full patient-specific simulation. Evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation across 12 skulls, it achieves a mean phase CMAE of 0.155 rad and amplitude rMAE of 9.089%, a focal centroid error of 0.467 mm, Dice score of 94.422%, and peak pressure ratio of 92.332%, with an approximately 2,535 times speedup over TR simulation. The code is available at https://github.com/Minju-Seol/fewshot-tfus-correction.
tldr: This paper proposes a few-shot deep learning framework that predicts phase and amplitude corrections for transcranial focused ultrasound from patient CT images, achieving high accuracy and a 2,535x speedup over conventional simulation, enabling real-time adaptive correction.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种少样本深度学习框架，从患者CT图像预测经颅聚焦超声的相位和振幅校正，实现了高精度和比传统模拟快2535倍的速度，支持实时自适应校正。
summary_zh: 经颅聚焦超声（tFUS）是一种通过颅骨传递聚焦声能以实现神经调控和治疗应用的非侵入性技术。然而，颅骨的异质结构会引发复杂且患者特定的相位和振幅畸变，导致声学焦点扭曲并偏离预定靶点，从而影响治疗效果与安全性。传统的时间反演（TR）仿真可校正这些畸变，但依赖计算成本高昂的全波求解器，难以用于实时操作和迭代治疗规划。我们提出一种小样本深度替代框架，能够从患者CT图像中预测针对96单元3D相控阵换能器的逐单元相位和振幅校正。该框架通过几何感知编码器提取共享的颅骨路径特征，并分别用于专用相位分类分支和振幅回归分支，其中相位周期性通过循环期望解码处理。该框架在多种颅骨几何结构上预训练，仅需十个靶点进行微调，即可快速适应未见过的患者，而无需完整的患者特异性仿真。基于12例颅骨的留一法交叉验证，该方法实现了平均相位平均绝对误差（CMAE）为0.155 rad，振幅相对平均绝对误差（rMAE）为9.089%，焦点质心误差为0.467 mm，Dice系数为94.422%，峰值压力比为92.332%，且计算速度较TR仿真提升约2535倍。代码见 https://github.com/Minju-Seol/fewshot-tfus-correction。

title: SCMA: Structure-Conditioned and Metal-Aware Flow Matching for CT Metal Artifact Reduction
summary: In X-ray CT, metallic objects cause beam hardening, photon starvation, and scattering, leading to projection inconsistency, streaks, dark bands, and structural distortions that compromise clinical diagnosis and quantitative analysis. Existing metal artifact reduction (MAR) methods remain limited: optimization-based methods may leave residual artifacts or blur structures, regression networks may generalize poorly across scenarios, and generative models without sample-specific structural guidance and physical constraints may produce anatomically inconsistent structures. Flow Matching learns a continuous-time velocity field that deterministically transports a source distribution to a target distribution, providing a flexible MAR prior. However, standard unconditional Flow Matching does not exploit sample-specific structure, spatially nonuniform metal-induced degradation, or measured projections. To address these limitations, we propose SCMA, a structure-conditioned and metal-aware Flow Matching framework. First, a linear-interpolation-corrected image is fed into the velocity network with the intermediate state as a sample-specific structural condition, guiding inference toward artifact-free CT images while preserving anatomy. Second, time-varying spatial weights from the metal mask and its distance transform are incorporated into the Flow Matching loss to emphasize severe degradation within and around metal regions. Finally, conditional Flow Matching updates alternate with projection-consistency correction during inference, allowing reliable measurements outside metal traces to constrain predictions. Experiments on simulated and real CT data demonstrate that SCMA more effectively suppresses metal artifacts, preserves local anatomical structures, and reduces hallucination-like structures inconsistent with projection measurements than representative MAR methods.
tldr: This paper proposes SCMA, a structure-conditioned and metal-aware Flow Matching framework for CT metal artifact reduction, which uses linear-interpolation-corrected images as structural guidance, time-varying spatial weights emphasizing metal regions, and projection-consistency correction during inference to suppress artifacts and preserve anatomy.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了SCMA，一种结构条件化和金属感知的流匹配框架，用于CT金属伪影减少。该框架利用线性插值校正图像作为结构指导，引入随时间变化的空间权重突出金属区域，并在推理过程中结合投影一致性校正，以抑制伪影并保留解剖结构。
summary_zh: 在X射线CT中，金属物体会导致射束硬化、光子饥饿和散射，进而引起投影不一致、条状伪影、暗带和结构变形，影响临床诊断和定量分析。现有的金属伪影减少（MAR）方法仍存在局限性：基于优化的方法可能残留伪影或模糊结构；回归网络在不同场景下泛化能力较差；而缺乏样本特定结构引导和物理约束的生成模型可能产生与解剖结构不一致的伪影。流匹配学习一个连续时间速度场，以确定性方式将源分布传输至目标分布，从而提供灵活的MAR先验。然而，标准无条件流匹配未能利用样本特定结构、空间非均匀的金属诱导退化或测量投影。为解决这些局限，我们提出SCMA——一种结构条件化且金属感知的流匹配框架。首先，将线性插值校正后的图像与中间状态共同输入速度网络，作为样本特定结构条件，引导推理向无伪影CT图像收敛，同时保留解剖结构。其次，将源自金属掩膜及其距离变换的时变空间权重引入流匹配损失函数，以强调金属区域及其内部的严重退化。最后，在推理过程中，条件流匹配更新与投影一致性校正交替进行，使得金属轨迹外的可靠测量值能够约束预测结果。在模拟和真实CT数据上的实验表明，与代表性MAR方法相比，SCMA能更有效地抑制金属伪影、保留局部解剖结构，并减少与投影测量不一致的幻觉样结构。

title: SAM+D: Parameter-Efficient Dimensional Lifting of SAM-Family Models via Depth-Routed LoRA and Depth Shifting
summary: Existing methods for adapting 2D foundation models such as SAM to 3D volumes either process slices independently---ignoring inter-slice context---or require substantial architectural changes and retraining. In this paper, we present \textbf{SAM+D}, a parameter-efficient framework that lifts SAM-family models by one spatial dimension---enabling 3D volumetric segmentation from 2D SAM and, for the first time via parameter-efficient fine-tuning, end-to-end 4D (3D+T) spatiotemporal segmentation from video-based SAM2---while keeping the vast majority of pre-trained parameters frozen. SAM+D introduces two lightweight, model-agnostic modules into frozen transformer blocks: (1)~\textbf{Depth-Routed LoRA (DRLoRA)} experts with learned routing for spatially adaptive low-rank updates, and (2)~\textbf{Depth Shift Modules (DSM)} for cross-slice feature exchange at zero additional parameter cost. Together, they provide volume-level context while tuning only ${\sim}$2.8\% of parameters for SAM and ${\sim}$3.7\% for SAM2. We evaluate SAM+D in two distinct settings, each lifting the base model by one spatial dimension: 3D segmentation, where SAM(2D$\,\to\,$3D) is evaluated on four CT benchmarks (KiTS, Pancreas, LiTS, Colon), and 4D segmentation, where SAM2 (2D+T$\,\to\,$3D+T) is evaluated on a cell tracking challenge (CTC) dataset (Fluo-N3DH-SIM+). In both settings SAM+D achieves competitive or superior results under the single-point prompt setting while using fewer trainable parameters than existing methods, demonstrating that SAM+D generalizes across SAM-family architectures, target dimensionalities (3D, 4D), and domains spanning medical imaging and bio-scene understanding. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/JerrySongCST/SAM-Plus-D.
tldr: SAM+D introduces two lightweight modules (Depth-Routed LoRA and Depth Shift Modules) to adapt 2D SAM-family models for 3D volumetric and 4D spatiotemporal segmentation with minimal trainable parameters, achieving competitive results on medical and bio-scene benchmarks.
tldr_zh: SAM+D 提出了两个轻量级模块（深度路由LoRA和深度移位模块），将2D SAM系列模型适配为3D体积和4D时空分割，仅需极少可训练参数，在医学和生物场景基准上取得有竞争力的结果。
summary_zh: 现有将SAM等二维基础模型适配到三维体数据的方法要么独立处理切片（忽略切片间上下文），要么需要大幅修改架构并重新训练。本文提出\textbf{SAM+D}——一种参数高效框架，可将SAM系列模型提升一个空间维度：从2D SAM实现3D体分割，并首次通过参数高效微调，从基于视频的SAM2实现端到端4D（3D+T）时空分割，同时冻结绝大多数预训练参数。SAM+D在冻结的Transformer块中引入两个轻量级、与模型无关的模块：（1）\textbf{深度路由LoRA（DRLoRA）}专家模块，通过学习的路由实现空间自适应低秩更新；（2）\textbf{深度移位模块（DSM）}，以零额外参数代价实现跨切片特征交换。两者共同提供体积级上下文，同时仅微调SAM约2.8%的参数和SAM2约3.7%的参数。我们在两种不同设置下评估SAM+D，每种设置均将基础模型提升一个空间维度：3D分割中，SAM（2D→3D）在四个CT基准数据集（KiTS、Pancreas、LiTS、Colon）上评估；4D分割中，SAM2（2D+T→3D+T）在细胞追踪挑战（CTC）数据集（Fluo-N3DH-SIM+）上评估。在两种设置下，SAM+D在单点提示场景下均达到具有竞争力甚至更优的结果，同时使用比现有方法更少的可训练参数，证明SAM+D可泛化至SAM系列架构、目标维度（3D、4D）以及医学影像与生物场景理解领域。代码已公开：https://github.com/JerrySongCST/SAM-Plus-D。

title: CyberNeuro: A Privacy-Preserving Agentic Workbench for Cohort-Scale Neuroimage and Clinical Data Analysis
summary: Despite tremendous success in neuroimaging methodology, making large-scale, high-dimensional datasets ready for AI/ML applications remains a critical operational bottleneck. Conventional workflows require extensive manual effort across metadata curation, pipeline execution, post-processing quality control, and data management, a burden that disproportionately excludes laboratories with limited manpower and computational infrastructure. To address this real-world barrier, there is an urgent need for scalable, cost-effective computational platforms that democratize advanced neuroimaging analytics and accelerate discoveries in mental health and clinical translation. Capitalizing on multi-agent LLM breakthroughs, we introduce CyberNeuro, an agentic workbench with a tailored local LLM-model ('WandaMind') for automated neuroimaging and health-data analysis. Driven by four dedicated agents (Planner, Validator, Dispatcher, and Reporter) communicating via a secure MCP bridge and a pinned execution layer, CyberNeuro enables researchers to execute complex workflows using natural language while maintaining clinical-grade data privacy. On the public NeuroBench suite, CyberNeuro increases held-out domain accuracy from 40% to 69% over the baseline model. Beyond automated metrics, the platform integrates a human-in-the-loop verification panel to ensure rigorous biomedical quality control. Across the same end-to-end 10-batch cohort workflow suite, the local WandaMind configuration completed all tasks with an estimated aggregate token count of about 10.6% using WandaMind and 61.7% using cloud providers of token usage, compared to Neuroclaw, respectively. The platform and its production-ready modules are available at https://wanda-cyberbench.com.
tldr: CyberNeuro is an agentic workbench leveraging a local LLM (WandaMind) and multi-agent architecture to automate neuroimaging and clinical data analysis workflows with privacy preservation, achieving significant accuracy improvements and reduced token usage compared to baselines.
tldr_zh: CyberNeuro 是一个利用本地大语言模型（WandaMind）和多智能体架构的智能工作台，用于自动化神经影像和临床数据分析流程，同时保护隐私，相比基线模型在准确性和令牌使用量上均有显著改进。
summary_zh: 尽管神经影像学方法取得了巨大成功，但使大规模高维数据集准备好用于人工智能/机器学习应用仍是一个关键的操作瓶颈。传统工作流程需要大量人工处理元数据整理、流程执行、后处理质量控制及数据管理，这一负担尤其使人力与计算基础设施有限的实验室难以承受。为应对这一现实障碍，亟需可扩展、高性价比的计算平台来普及高级神经影像分析，加速精神健康领域的发现与临床转化。利用多智能体大语言模型的突破，我们推出了CyberNeuro——一个配备定制本地大语言模型（"WandaMind"）的智能体工作台，用于自动化神经影像与健康数据分析。该系统由四个专用智能体（规划器、验证器、调度器与报告器）驱动，通过安全的MCP桥接与固定执行层进行通信，使研究者能够使用自然语言执行复杂工作流程，同时保持临床级数据隐私。在公开的NeuroBench测试套件上，CyberNeuro将基线模型的领域外准确率从40%提升至69%。除自动化指标外，该平台集成了人在回路验证面板，以确保严格的生物医学质量控制。在相同的端到端10批次队列工作流程套件中，与Neuroclaw相比，本地WandaMind配置以估计总令牌数完成所有任务：使用WandaMind约为10.6%，使用云提供商约为61.7%。该平台及其生产就绪模块可通过https://wanda-cyberbench.com获取。
